text:
Maya G: Heads-up — prepping partner QBR packs for next week. Need final partner tier rubrics + proposed MDF splits for cloud marketplace and HW partners. Can folks drop variance numbers by EOD?

Omar Khan: I can run the marketplace numbers. Will surface delta vs last Q (ARR influenced). Quick q: do we target top 10 partners only or QBR set + tier review?

Maya G: QBR set + any partners on the cusp of promotion/demotion. Want the rubric to justify tier moves.

Sarah P: Adding rubric draft below. It's light but actionable. Feedback welcome.

Sarah P: ```
Tier eval components:
- Revenue contribution (30%)
- Joint pipeline strength (20%)
- Technical integrations (performance/compatibility) (15%)
- Marketplace presence (listings + certification) (15%)
- GTM activity & co-marketing (10%)
- Support SLAs / escalations resolved (10%)
Scoring: 0-5 per category, weighted sum. Promotion threshold = weighted score >= 4.0
```

Alex R: Love the weights. Suggest bumping Technical integrations to 20% and lowering marketplace to 10% for HW-first partners. Also we should have a binary check for compliance/security for Private deployments — automatic veto if not met.

Maya G: Agree on the compliance veto. For MDF splits: propose baseline pool = 8% of forecasted partner-driven ARR, with bonus slices for strategic marketplace placements and co-sell commitments.

Omar Khan: Running a quick simulation: with baseline 8% pool, top-5 partners consume ~55% of MDF in conservative model. If we add hw-partner premium (+5ppt) we hit >70% concentration. Do we want that?

Sarah P: Not ideal. Can we set a cap per partner (e.g., 25% of pool) and an exceptions committee for strategic cases? Keeps runway for long-tail partners.

Maya G: Yes cap at 25% makes sense. Add exceptions with 2/3 approval from partnerships leads + finance review.

PartnerBot: Reminder — previous QBR templates (2025-Q4) and MDF ledger are in /shared/partnerships/qbr-archive. I can attach links if needed. :link:

Alex R: Can someone owner the rubric doc and produce a redline with the HW adjustments? I'll own the exceptions workflow doc for finance sign-off.

Maya G: Alex, can you own the rubric redline? Omar, run the MDF sims and post 3 scenarios (8% baseline, 6% conservative, 10% aggressive) with partner caps applied. Sarah, please finalize the rubric language and add compliance veto clause.

Omar Khan: On it — will post sims by 17:30 PT.

Sarah P: I'll drop updated rubric + sample scoring spreadsheet before EOD.

Maya G: Great. One last ask — for the QBR slides, include one slide that maps tier changes to expected latency/cost improvements for partners that adopt our Dedicated offering. Helps tie product to partner outcomes.

Alex R: Noted. I'll add a slide template with a short matrix (tier vs expected uplift).

Maya G: Thanks team. Quick async check-in later if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
